title: 10 AI PROMPTS
THAT *WRITE*
YOUR REELS
subtitle: Give AI direction, not a task.
tagline: Prompt 01 wrote our reel, word for word.

blocks.heading: How to *use* these
blocks.intro: A lazy prompt gets you "Hey guys, in today's video...", the same script everyone else is posting. Each prompt here gives the AI a role, an audience, a hook rule, a format and a tone, so it knows who it's writing for, what to say and how to say it.
steps: Open a fresh chat in ChatGPT. They also work in Gemini and Claude.
Replace everything in [brackets] with your own details. The more specific, the better: [creators under 10K who post but don't grow] beats [creators].
If it sounds generic, reply: "Too generic. No greetings. Make the first line a surprising claim."
Cut any line you wouldn't say to a friend, then film.
blocks.note: Tip: stay in the same chat for prompts 02 to 10, so the AI remembers your niche, audience and tone from prompt 01.

items.line: Role: You're a short-form scriptwriter for [type of creator]. Audience: [who you help]. Hook rule: The first line must stop the scroll. No greetings. Format: [28] seconds, [problem, mistake, fix, call to action]. Tone: [Talk like a friend, not a teacher]. Task: Write the voiceover for a reel about [topic]. Only the spoken lines, no emojis.
items.example: "This reel was written by ChatGPT. And honestly, that's the point." The exact prompt behind our reel.
items.why: Five parts turn a task into direction: the AI knows who it is, who it's talking to and what to say.

items.line: Write [10] opening lines for a reel about [topic] for [audience]. Each under [12] words. No greetings, no "in today's video". Mix a surprising claim, a mistake they make, a result and a question. Rank them by how hard they'd stop the scroll.
items.example: "You're not bad at Instagram. Your first two seconds are."
items.why: The hook decides if anyone hears the rest. Ten options beat one guess.

items.line: Write a [30]-second reel script about [my experience] using this structure: something relatable, then the conflict, then the realisation, then what I do now. End with: Comment [KEYWORD] and I'll send you [free resource].
items.example: "You post a reel, and then you refresh. Every five minutes."
items.why: Story structure keeps people watching to find out how it ends.

items.line: Here are [3] captions I wrote: [paste captions]. Describe my tone in 5 words. Then rewrite this script so it sounds like me: [paste script]. Keep my slang, cut anything I'd never say.
items.example: Tone: blunt, funny, short sentences, a bit sarcastic, no fluff.
items.why: AI scripts sound like AI until you show it how you actually talk.

items.line: Write a [25]-second reel: "[number] [things] that [result] for [audience]". One line per item, each with a quick why. Put the strongest item first and save a surprising one for last.
items.example: "3 openers that kill your reel in two seconds."
items.why: Lists are easy to follow, save and share.

items.line: For this script: [paste script], write the on-screen text for each line. Max [6] words per screen, one key word to highlight per line, and a first-frame title that makes sense with the sound off.
items.example: First frame: "AI wrote this reel". Highlight: AI.
items.why: Most people watch muted at first. The text has to hook them alone.

items.line: Act as a viewer who scrolls fast. Read this script: [paste script]. Tell me the exact line where you'd scroll away and why. Then rewrite only that part so you'd keep watching.
items.example: "I'd leave at line 2: it explains before it shows. Lead with the result instead."
items.why: Catch the boring part before you film, not after it flops.

items.line: Here's the transcript of my long video: [paste transcript]. Pull out [3] moments that work as standalone reels. For each: a hook, a [20]-second script and on-screen text.
items.example: One podcast episode, three reels: a hot take, a story and a quick tip.
items.why: You already have the content. AI finds the clips worth posting.

items.line: Write an Instagram caption for this reel: [paste script]. Start with: Comment [KEYWORD] and I'll send you [resource]. Then 3 short lines that use the phrases people search for, like [search phrases]. No emojis, 5 hashtags at the end.
items.example: "Comment PROMPT and I'll send you the exact ChatGPT prompt that wrote this reel."
items.why: The first line drives comments; the search phrases help new people find you.

items.line: My niche is [niche] and my audience is [audience]. Give me [30] reel ideas: 10 mistakes, 10 quick wins and 10 stories or opinions. For each, one hook line and the format (talking head, list, demo or story).
items.example: Mistake: "Stop opening with 'hey guys'." Format: list.
items.why: A month planned in one chat means you never stare at a blank screen at 9 PM.

blocks.heading: Before you *post*
items: The first line works without a greeting
The first frame makes sense with the sound off
Every line sounds like you said it out loud
One idea per reel, not three
It ends with one clear action: comment, save or follow
Your caption starts with the keyword and uses search phrases
